newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary research sees milestone in gene therapy.
newsitem.headline: Hungary research sees milestone in gene therapy.

text.p: Artificial mammal chromosomes, developed by Hungarian scientists, could revolutionise gene therapy, the Hungarian news agency MTI said on Friday.
The artificial chromosomes have been developed by researchers of the Hungarian Academy of Science in the southern Hungarian town Szeged.

Henry R Geraedst, chairman of CHROMOS Molecular Systems, a company founded in Canada for the further development and utilisation of the Hungarian invention, told MTI that the chromosomes may be made suitable for transporting controllable genetical information into cells.
The research, if successful, would be a milestone in biotechnology and gene therapy, MTI said.
